findings.reason: the section must name routing's selection as retired (the gate delegating its record choice to `read_plan_review`), or it lands two owners of the same rule.
findings.text: `require_plan_reviewed` selects the record the gate checks with `record = max(records, key=lambda item: int(item.get("plan_version") or 0))` over `_review_coverage`'s contributing list, while §23 re-expresses `read_plan_review` as "the newest stored review among those the predicate counts as covering, the record whose findings the gate checks"; the plan asserts "the gate, the answer verb and the view read one record by one rule" but leaves routing's own `max()` in place as a second owner of that selection, so the two drift the moment one is fixed

findings.reason: the sections should either promote these helpers or give them one home rather than repeat the cross-module private read the project has already flagged and had to repair.
findings.text: the plan reads `dispatch._normalised_words`, a private module-level function, from `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` (§22) and proposes a private snapshot-name constant in `plan_review.py` read by recovery's writer (§21), justifying both as same-package; but the project treats a private name read across a module boundary as a defect even within `reckon.crew` — the §6 re-review already recorded `reckon/crew/recovery.py:581` reading `plan_review._REVIEW_SIDECAR_NAME` as a follow-on — so the modules are shallower than "hides behaviour behind a smaller interface" claims; the honest change is one home for the tokeniser and the snapshot name (promote, or relocate beside their consumers)

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the plan keeps two helpers private while reading them across module boundaries, so the interface is not the boundary the plan claims (`dispatch._normalised_words`, and the proposed snapshot-name constant), the exact pattern the project already flagged at `reckon/crew/recovery.py:581`.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §23 re-expresses `read_plan_review` to return "the newest stored review… the record whose findings the gate checks", a second owner of the coverage-record selection that `reckon/crew/routing.py:2667` already performs, and the plan does not name the gate's selection as retired.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; every section that adds surface names its retirement in its own text (§16 second node retires interim `strip_tags` for `section_prose`, net +1 and verified uncounted constants as the family defines them; §22 retires `plan_review_settle_seconds` for `plan_review_settings`; §23 retires `store_delivered_report` to private for `store_delivered_reviews`; §21 adds and retires nothing), and no section adds a CLI option, MCP view or refusal family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan censuses every proposed mechanism's sites before adding one (the 14-line `stripped_strings|get_text(` census it classifies by kind, the `"plan-review"` report-root spelled twice at `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:795` and `:866`, `impl_source` in neither scalar set) and names the owner each section extends (`roadmap.implementable_sections`, `is_..._section`, `dispatch._normalised_words`, `review_report_directory`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one hoist, `store_delivered_reviews`, moves `routing._store_delivered_plan_review` to the module that already owns `store_delivered_report` and `delivered_reports` and states why (two callers, `grep` for the old name returns nothing), and `plan_review_settings` replaces rather than sits beside `plan_review_settle_seconds`.
